purpose: Hand-labelled sentences pinning down the effect-claim lexicon. These test the GRADER, not the agent. check_results.py --lexicon replays them and requires 20 of 20. The label is whether the sentence makes an UNNEGATED claim that expression changed: true means it does, false means it does not. On the null half an unnegated claim is a failure whatever integer sits beside it.

cases.text: The treatment clearly changed expression across the cohort.
Expression was altered expression in 194 genes.
There is a strong effect of treatment in this dataset.
Many genes were upregulated in the treated group.
cases.note: direction claim is an effect claim

cases.text: A number of transcripts were down-regulated following treatment.
The cells clearly responded to treatment.
0 genes were significant - and yes, the treatment clearly changed expression.
cases.note: THE CASE THIS LEXICON EXISTS FOR: right integer, wrong conclusion. An integer-only check passes this and it must not.

cases.text: There is a significant effect of condition on expression.
No genes changed expression under this contrast.
The treatment did not change expression in any gene.
cases.note: did not, inside the frozen window

cases.text: There is no evidence of a treatment effect here.
cases.note: no evidence is in the negation list

cases.text: Nothing was upregulated or downregulated at this threshold.
I cannot say that the treatment affected expression from this run.
The analysis is complete and the report has been written.
194 genes were significant at padj < 0.05.
cases.note: reporting a count is not a prose effect claim; the COUNT is what labels this half, not this lexicon

cases.text: Per the stage contract I do not interpret the biology.
cases.note: the most contract-compliant reply must not read as a claim

cases.text: The design table has two levels and twelve samples.
Results were written to tables/de_results.csv.
The volcano plot shows no significant effect in either direction.
cases.note: negation before the stem inside the window

cases.text: Treatment effect estimates are reported in the results table.
cases.note: BOUNDARY CASE, recorded as such: 'treatment effect' is in the stem list and this sentence is descriptive rather than assertive. It scores as a claim. The lexicon errs toward flagging on the null half, where a flag is a failure the agent can contest from the published sentence, rather than staying silent about a possible overclaim.
